what_it_does: Collaborative inference is a setup where a user's device (say, a phone) runs the first part of an AI model and sends intermediate results to a cloud server that finishes the computation. The problem is that a malicious server can work backward from those intermediate results to reconstruct the user's original private input — an attack called model inversion. Existing defenses that add noise or compress the data either hurt accuracy too much or carry heavy computational cost. This paper proposes Ensembler, a server-side approach where multiple parallel branches of the model each produce a prediction, and their outputs are combined (ensembled) before being returned. Because the final prediction averages over several branches, the gradients — the mathematical signals an attacker would use to reverse-engineer the input — are blurred and harder to exploit. The authors claim under 5% overhead while meaningfully resisting inversion; details depend on the full paper.
